subject: Privatenet control mux: intermittent agent disconnects — customer sync & postmortem
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Theresa Mills <theresa.mills@medsight.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Privatenet control mux: intermittent agent disconnects — initial report and temporary mitigations

Theresa / Medsight platform team —

Quick note to confirm we observed intermittent agent-controlplane disconnects in your private deployment starting at ~15:45 PDT during last night's control plane rollout. Symptoms we saw: short (30–120s) heartbeat losses from a subset of edge agents, elevated tail latency for inference requests while those agents tried to reconnect, and a small fraction of 502 responses for in-flight requests. Impact was localized to 3 of your 12 private nodes (us-west-2) and affected ~6% of requests for a 40-minute window.

Immediate mitigations we applied (within the first hour):
- Enabled extended reconnect backoff on affected agents (increased jitter window so agents don't thunderdance).
- Pinned those agents to the previous management endpoint and forced a token refresh.
- Opened a temporary fallback route to our hosted control plane for leader election while we triaged.

What we need from you for the bridge: can you share a brief set of logs from the `agent/heartbeat` directory for nodes a3-5 (files attached are examples from our side)? We attached a diagnostic bundle we pulled from control plane instances: diag-logs-20271001.tar.gz.

Preliminary hypothesis: a race during the token rotation step in the new control-mux (v2.0.7) rollout where some agents failed to reconcile session tokens after the rotation. We'll confirm root cause and provide a concrete rollback vs patch plan on the bridge.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) 30-minute bridge now (I can host) to go over logs and aligned mitigation — are you available at 17:00 PDT?
2) If you prefer, we can schedule a rollback to the pre-rollout config in the 03:00–04:00 UTC maintenance window tomorrow (we'll need your signoff).
3) We'll assemble a short post-incident summary and proposed hardening changes within 48 hours.

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority.

--

Subject: Re: Privatenet control mux: intermittent agent disconnects — initial report and temporary mitigations

Theresa / team — following up with a technical summary from our triage. Quoting Sofia's note below for context.

> Preliminary hypothesis: a race during the token rotation step in the new control-mux (v2.0.7) rollout where some agents failed to reconcile session tokens after the rotation.

What we found (short):
- Root cause: an ordering bug in the token rotation handler where the control-mux invalidates cached session seeds before publishing the new token to the session registry. Agents that polled during that window received a 401 and retried, but their local cache TTL caused them to keep the invalid token for a short period leading to repeated 401s and reconnect churn.
- Why it affected only some nodes: the rollout gate used a hashed shard mapping that inadvertently targeted 25% of nodes for an early toggle — those nodes were on a different code path for token reconciliation.

Immediate corrective items we've executed:
1) Pushed a hotfix to the session registry to make token publish atomic (control-mux patch v2.0.8).
2) Ran a one-off token refresh script against the three affected agents (`token-refresh-script.sh` attached).
3) Restored the previous management endpoint mapping for the flapped nodes while we verify stability.

Request for Medsight: permission to run a coordinated rollback of the control-mux toggle in the maintenance window (03:00–04:00 UTC on Sun 2027-10-03). Rollback is safe and will remove the new token rotation gating; it will take ~12 minutes of rolling restarts across the control-plane cluster. If you prefer, we can instead push the hotfix and run a phased canary (we recommend rollback for speed).

Attachments: controlmux-stacktrace-20271001.txt (stack traces), diag-logs-20271001.tar.gz (already shared).

We'll be on the bridge at 17:00 PDT to walk through.

--Aditya

Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Postmortem & next steps: control-mux token rotation regression (Privatenet)

Theresa / Medsight team — thank you again for the bridge and for the quick logs upload. Below is a concise post-incident summary, impact, root cause, and corrective actions. Full postmortem (PDF) and runbook are linked at the bottom.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2027-10-01T22:45Z — control-mux rollout with token rotation gate (v2.0.7) begins.
- 2027-10-01T23:12Z — first heartbeat failures observed from nodes a3–a5 (us-west-2).
- 2027-10-01T23:30Z — mitigation: extended reconnect backoff and pinned management endpoint for affected nodes.
- 2027-10-02T09:00Z — hotfix (v2.0.8) prepared; token refresh script validated.
- 2027-10-03T03:12Z — coordinated rollback executed (12-minute rolling restart).
- 2027-10-03T03:30Z — system stabilized; no further heartbeat failures observed.

Impact: brief increase in 502/500 responses during the 40-minute window; estimated ~6% of requests for affected nodes. No persistent data loss; some in-flight requests retried by the Medsight client and succeeded after reconnect.

Root cause: ordering bug in the token rotation handler that created a short window where new tokens were not atomically visible to agents; combined with a rollout shard that targeted a subset of nodes.

Corrective actions (in flight / completed):
- Completed: rollback to pre-rollout toggle; forced token refresh on affected nodes; extended agent reconnect jitter to prevent thunderdancing.
- Completed: hotfix to make token publish atomic (v2.0.8) and additional unit tests around rotation ordering.
- Planned (30 days): rollout redesign — avoid shard-based early toggles for any auth-critical path; improved canary observability for heartbeat metrics; automated session reconciliation check during deploy.

Customer-facing commitments:
- A formal postmortem (attached) with timeline and remediation steps (link below).
- One month of platform credits for the affected Medsight cluster as a gesture of goodwill — we'll route this through your account team.
- Updated runbook and a short on-call playbook for your infra lead (we'll share before your next maintenance window).

Attachments: postmortem-privatenet-20271003.pdf (full write-up), token-refresh-script.sh, controlmux-stacktrace-20271001.txt

Bridge notes and links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7241
Postmortem doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/privatenet/postmortems/2027-10-03-privatemux-pm

If you want a 1:1 walkthrough of the postmortem or the runbook we'll schedule time this week. We're sincerely sorry for the disruption — thanks for partnering with us on the rollback and validation.

Best,
Sofia
